study_design: Hospital-based comparative observational study of newly diagnosed prostate cancer patients and healthy controls
cohort_total_n_excerpt: A total of 80 prostate cancer patients and 80 controls were included.
reason: The study compares serum micronutrient levels in newly diagnosed general prostate cancer patients and healthy controls. It provides no aggressive prostate cancer analysis.

estimate_classifications.endpoint_excerpt: Magnesium levels were slightly higher in cases but not statistically significant.
estimate_classifications.reason: This is a serum magnesium comparison between general prostate cancer cases and controls, not an aggressive-incidence estimate.

estimate_classifications.endpoint_excerpt: Conversely, serum copper (129.13 ± 22.41 mcg/dl), iron (145.44 ± 39.41 mcg/dl), and calcium (9.50 ± 1.01 mcg/dl) were significantly elevated in cases (p < 0.05).
estimate_classifications.reason: This is a serum iron comparison involving general prostate cancer cases; no aggressive endpoint is defined.

estimate_classifications.endpoint_excerpt: Prostate cancer patients exhibited significantly lower serum selenium (82.50 ± 16.76 mcg/L) and zinc (56.98 ± 15.25 mcg/dl) levels compared to controls (p < 0.05).
